# 4 Maccabees Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Remaining Brothers and the Mother

---

**1** After the sixth had also died in blessed death following all his sufferings, the seventh and youngest came forward.

**2** The tyrant, moved with compassion for the boy's youth, called him close and urged him to have pity on himself and not to share in his brothers' madness — that he should abandon his ancestral customs and live among the Greeks.

**3** But the youth replied: I am the last of my brothers; I will not bring shame upon my brothers by refusing to share in their suffering, and I will resist you just as they did.

**4** What you are doing to me is not justice but cruelty; you are forcing unlawful food upon me in order to get me to betray God.

**5** You cannot compel me by any argument or any force; for I am governed by holy reason and am worthy of my brothers.

**6** My brothers, having endured a brief pain, have now tasted of ever-flowing life under God's covenant; but you, through the judgment of God, will receive just punishment for your arrogance.

**7** I, like my brothers, surrender both body and life for the ancestral laws, praying to God that he will quickly show mercy to our nation.

**8** And I pray that through me and my brothers the wrath of the Almighty, which has justly fallen upon our whole people, may be brought to an end.

**9** As for me, I surrender my body and soul into the hands of God, calling out to him in prayer: O Lord, I am brought before you and I offer you my blood as a purification — and let this be sufficient on behalf of our nation.

**10** When he had said this, they tortured him even more cruelly than the others, furious at his contempt for them.

**11** This was in keeping with his noble character, for he had been formed in the same philosophy of courage as his brothers.

**12** And so, having committed his whole soul to God, he died nobly in his torments, like another Eleazar.

**13** After all the brothers had died, their mother was the last to be put to death.

**14** The mother of the seven merits praise surpassing every commendation of heroism; for she, while watching the murder of seven sons within the space of a single day, bore it with good courage because of her hope in God.

**15** She exhorted each of them in the language of their fathers; filled with a noble spirit she fired her woman's reasoning with a manly courage and said to them:

**16** I was a pure virgin and did not step beyond the walls of my father's house; and I did not know the pleasures of this world.

**17** I kept myself in chastity and I did not transgress my God's commandments, nor is there any sin known to me.

**18** I say before my children: God has not given me another son; I know no other son, for he has taken from me each of those who should have been memorials of his holy name.

**19** Therefore this is my supreme joy: that having given birth to and reared these holy sons I see not one of them separated from the purpose of God.
